subject: Lumina Health POC: prompt capture playbook & QA matrix
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@luminahealth.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@luminahealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina Health POC: prompt capture playbook & QA matrix

Hi Sophie / Rajiv —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a concrete ask to keep momentum for the POC (3–4 week trial):

Recap
- Goal: Validate that Redwood reduces inference cost by >=25% at target latency while preserving >92% accuracy on clinical triage prompts.
- Scope: 10k prompt-eval pairs for initial evaluation (see sampling note below); model family: LlamaX-70b quantized variant (Redwood will propose runtime profile).
- Timeline: sample delivery by end of next week, initial eval by week 2 of the trial, customer-facing demo week 3.

Immediate ask (what we need from Lumina)
1) Prompt set: a CSV of representative prompts (one per row) with an associated label/expected output where possible. Ideally 8k–12k rows; if not available, a rolling delivery is OK.
2) Privacy/PII flagging: flag any prompts containing PHI or patient identifiers. If you cannot flag, we can supply an anonymization script — but we need confirmation of which fields we should scrub.
3) Success criteria: please confirm top-3 success metrics from your side (suggested: accuracy vs. gold labels, mean latency at p95, and false-positive rate on triage escalation).
4) Ownership & contacts: who on your side will own prompt delivery, approvals, and DPA signoff?

Attachments: Redwood_POC_requirements_v1.pdf (high-level checklist + CSV template).

Next steps from Redwood: we’ll provide a short-playbook for sampling, an anonymization helper (+ Docker), and a QA matrix that maps prompt categories to test cases.

Can you confirm you can deliver an initial sample (at least 2k prompts) by EOD next Friday (2028-04-27)? If that’s tight, tell us the earliest feasible date and we’ll adapt the POC plan.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a trial.

— Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@luminahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@luminahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health POC: prompt capture playbook & QA matrix

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear recap. We can start with a first batch.

What we can deliver this week
- A 2,100-row CSV export from our support triage system (anonymized to remove patient IDs) — attached as Lumina_sample_prompts_20280420.csv. The CSV includes: prompt_text, channel, triage_label, created_at.
- A short README explaining our internal labels and a note about how triage_label maps to clinician escalation.

Notes / constraints
- The CSV has been through our initial redaction, but we still have free-text clinician notes that may contain PHI. If Redwood can run an additional pass with your anonymization script, that would be helpful.
- Our security team will need the DPA & data flow diagram for the Private deployment option. Rajiv is copying procurement and security.

Success criteria (from our side) — tentative
1) >=90% alignment with our gold labels on the 2k baseline set
2) p95 latency < 800ms for 1k qps test profile (we can scale down the qps for the POC)
3) No >0.5% critical misclassification that routes patients to high-priority escalation incorrectly

We’ll push the initial CSV to your shared Drive folder and confirm by EOD.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Tran
Head of Clinical Product
Lumina Health
sophie.tran@luminahealth.com

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Lumina Health POC: prompt capture playbook & QA matrix

Thanks Sophie — that export is great and a good starting point. A few clarifying items so we can finalize the eval plan and lock timeline: 

1) Sampling & dataset split - We recommend the following split for the 2.1k sample while we collect the larger 10k: 60% train-like (for model adaptation, if you want), 20% validation (for early checks), 20% holdout (for final pass). If you don’t want adaptation, we’ll treat all as evaluation.

2) Anonymization workflow - We’ll run our anonymization helper (Docker image) as a non-destructive pass and provide a diff/report of redacted tokens. Please confirm if Lumina is comfortable with Redwood running this job in your S3 bucket / an SFTP drop. Alternatively, we can supply the script for your infra team to run.

3) QA matrix (what we’ll test)
- Category coverage: clinical-intake, follow-up-requests, medication-queries, 'unknown' phrasing, multi-turn escalation cases. - Edge-case tests: shorthand, misspellings, merged fields in notes, punctuation-heavy entries. - Safety tests: PII leakage, hallucination risk on patient-sensitive prompts.

4) Ownership & timeline - Owner for prompt delivery (Lumina): Sophie (clinical product) — confirm? - Security/contact for DPA & deployment: Rajiv (copied). - Redwood owners: Karthik (data ingestion & eval infra), Vivek (trial config & runtime profile).

5) Acceptance criteria — Redwood proposal (we shared this to align, please confirm):
- Primary metric: label alignment >= 90% on holdout set- Secondary: p95 latency < 800ms at 200 qps profile- Blocker: >0.5% critical misclassification triggers escalation and ends POC

Please confirm ownership and whether you want Redwood to run anonymization in your environment (we prefer customer-run if you have strong controls). Once we have that we’ll post the formal eval plan and milestone dates to the Drive folder and set the kickoff for 2028-05-01.

— Monica

Confirming:
- Sophie is owner for dataset context and label mapping.
- I’ll coordinate our security review and send the DPA + network diagram by Wednesday (2028-04-25).
- We prefer to run the anonymization script in our environment. Please share the Docker image & instructions and we’ll run it against the current CSV.

Small ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist of minimum metadata columns you need (we saw prompt_text, channel, triage_label, created_at; anything else helpful?) If possible include a sample manifest mapping field names to expected formats (CSV header -> example).

Subject: Internal: Lumina POC next steps (owners & deliverables)

Vivek / Karthik — moving this thread internal briefly to confirm our deliverables based on Lumina's replies. I’ll leave external parties on copy for transparency.

Deliverables / owners (Redwood):
- Ingest manifest & CSV template (Karthik) — deliver by 2028-04-24 EOD. Include optional fields: user_id_hash, session_id, free_text_notes.
- Anonymization helper + Docker image & README (Karthik) — provide image tag and instructions by 2028-04-24. Lumina will run in their environment.
- Eval plan & QA matrix (Vivek) — draft and post to Drive by 2028-04-26. Include the category coverage and edge-case tests.
- Runtime test profile & cost estimate (Vivek) — provide expected token counts and a 200 qps latency run estimate by 2028-04-26.
- SOW / POC pricing stub (monica) — draft and share with procurement by 2028-04-25.

Notes: keep the acceptance criteria conservative (>=90% alignment, p95 <800ms) but we’ll be ready to iterate. I’ll drive the kickoff scheduling for 2028-05-01 once Karthik confirms ingest artifacts are ready.

— Monica
